payload.root_cause_why_p8_failed: The architect's diagnosis was WRONG. 'no such column: created_at' is a column-EXISTENCE drift, NOT a missing-DEFAULT problem. A missing DEFAULT on a NOT NULL column produces a CONSTRAINT error ('NOT NULL constraint failed') on INSERT, not 'no such column' on SELECT/query. The created_at x3 errors mean some table is being CREATED (and winning the IF NOT EXISTS race on the fresh :memory: singleton) by a DDL that OMITS the created_at column entirely — a competing/drifted CREATE TABLE elsewhere (production sibling slice, a P4 per-file inline-DDL fixture, or a test helper). Adding DEFAULT to the canonical DDL cannot help when a column-less DDL creates the table first. The self-heal DIRECTION is sound and reproducibly heals the table-MISSING classes (P5 and P8 both healed the same 4); it is the created_at column-EXISTENCE collision that nets it negative.
